display_name: Dual-phase xenon S1/S2 event formation and pairing

physics_grounding.basis: HC-DU-183 predates the atlas and reconstructs accepted dual-phase-xenon detector, triggerless-DAQ, event-building, and accidental-coincidence physics from collaboration sources, while separately proving the finite matching boundary.

source_bindings.native_claim_status: SOURCE-PINNED DETECTOR PACKET AND EXACT PAIRING BOUNDARY
source_bindings.native_evidence_grade: GRADE 4 EXACT PAIRING BOUNDARY; CONDITIONAL GRADE 3 RECONSTRUCTION; GRADE 2 SOURCE AUDIT
source_bindings.receiver_paraphrase: S1 and S2 may each be formed and retained records while their common-occurrence relation remains a separate physical or inferential record duty.
source_nonclaims: No novel detector theorem, new physics, zero-error source certificate, response-order discriminator, paper seed, or successor selection is established.
missing_import_requirements: No one numerically frozen apparatus regime is supplied across the XENON1T, XENONnT, and PandaX-II source packet.

physics.empirical_signature: An interaction in dual-phase liquid xenon can produce prompt scintillation S1 and delayed ionization-electroluminescence S2; a correctly associated pair conditionally reconstructs drift depth, while unrelated signals inside the drift window can form accidental coincidences.
accepted_frameworks: electron drift, extraction, and proportional scintillation
governing_relations: prompt excitation and scintillation form S1
ionization electrons drift, extract, and form delayed S2
z equals calibrated drift velocity times the correctly paired S2-minus-S1 delay
physically admissible S1/S2 relations form a bipartite compatibility graph
an exact pairing-dependent target factors the raw packet if and only if it is constant over every admissible-matching fibre
physics.validity_regime: Family-level dual-phase-xenon architecture under an above-threshold triggerless-acquisition contract, calibrated clock and drift response, target-blind pairing constraints, and a declared accidental-coincidence model. The source packet composes XENON1T detector physics, XENONnT acquisition/reconstruction, and PandaX-II accidental-coincidence evidence rather than freezing one numerical apparatus.
grounding_gaps: Detector dimensions, field strengths, temperature and pressure, electron lifetime, diffusion, digitization thresholds, event rates, calibration epoch, and event-class cuts are not numerically frozen into one apparatus packet.
The exact finite matching fixture establishes factorization logic, not the frequency of ambiguity in any collaboration data set.

initial_conditions.statement: The xenon target is maintained in a dual-phase liquid-gas configuration with fields sufficient for electron drift, extraction, and gas electroluminescence.
An admitted energy-deposition interaction occurs in the active liquid and can produce both excitation and ionization channels.
Clock, drift velocity, sensor response, and geometry calibrations are available for the declared run class.
The event-building interval may contain more than one acquired S1 candidate and more than one acquired S2 candidate.

boundary_conditions.statement: Only signals above the declared digitization and reconstruction thresholds enter the retained packet.
Candidate S1/S2 edges satisfy declared drift-time and quality constraints that are target-blind with respect to the chosen matching.
The interaction, drift path, liquid-gas interface, and sensor response lie inside the calibrated active-volume geometry.
No single collaboration-specific numerical detector configuration is selected by this family-level card.

evidence.ceiling_reason: HC-DU-183 supplies independent accepted detector grounding, primary-source reconstruction, accidental-coincidence evidence, and an exact finite factorization control; the v0.2 card is a non-routing typed mapping and imports no source Grade 4 promotion.

strongest_absorber.condition: Standard dual-phase-xenon detector physics, triggerless DAQ, calibrated stochastic event building, accidental-coincidence estimation, bipartite matching, and sufficient-statistic theory explain the entire packet.
strongest_absorber.consequence: The card earns no new detector physics or Dynamic Unity mechanism.

representation_kill.condition: The mapping collapses the underlying interaction, endpoint records, common-occurrence relation, pairing estimate, and certificate into one linear record or treats an immutable packet as a final event partition.
representation_kill.consequence: The representation contradicts the exact HC-DU-183 factorization boundary.

claim_falsifier.condition: A source-pinned theorem or exhaustive physical constraint shows that every physically realizable raw-packet fibre in the declared family is target-constant for event membership and paired depth.
claim_falsifier.consequence: The claimed nonfactorization and physical pairing remainder fail for that declared family.

regime_reopener.condition: A retained common-occurrence tag is added, a source-justified low-rate or topology class becomes uniquely matchable, or the detector, thresholds, calibration, event-rate model, or target changes.
regime_reopener.consequence: Recompute the compatibility graph and target constancy; this repairs or changes the regime rather than falsifying the conditional theorem.

held_out_discriminator.description: Before revealing event labels in a source-owned held-out packet class, freeze the compatibility graph and predict whether raw records uniquely factor pairing and paired depth.
opposed_outcomes: Every packet is target-constant under the frozen graph, so the pairing remainder is absent in that class.
At least one equal-record fibre contains target-varying admissible histories, so the pairing remainder survives.
